title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Economics (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Economics (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: A condition under which the market price of the commodity serves as a measure of what people are willing to pay?
options: There is no rationing of scales or price controls in the market for the good
Intervention in and failures of goods markets including the markets for internationally traded goods.
There is no consumer's surplus from the consumption of the good
There is a monopsony buyer who is large enough to force the project to sell its output below the price that the monopsonist is really willing to pay.
questions.explanation: In a free market without rationing or price controls, the market price accurately reflects willingness to pay. Price controls and rationing distort this relationship.

questions.questionText: Investment is defined as______?
options: flow of output that is used to maintain or increase capital stock of an economy in a given period of time
stock of output that is used to maintain or increase capital stock of an economy in a given period of time
stock of output that is used to maintain or decrease capital stock of an economy in a given period of time
flow of output that is used to maintain or decrease capital stock of an economy in a given period of time
questions.explanation: Investment is a flow variable (not a stock) that represents the rate at which new capital is being added to the existing capital stock over a specific time period. This includes expenditures on new capital goods or enhancing existing capital.

questions.questionText: The Mercantilists view on trade may be summarized by?
options: Enhancement of free trade
Restricting the use of gold and silver in trade
Advocacy of trade restriction
Focus on expansion of imports
questions.explanation: Mercantilists advocated for trade restrictions and protectionist policies to maintain a positive balance of trade, accumulate precious metals (gold and silver), and increase national wealth. They favored exports over imports and believed wealth was finite.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following statement is correct about cost?
options: TFC declines continuously as the level of firm's output increases.
Implicit costs are the costs of factors of production owned by the firm.
Decreasing costs refers to the situation wherein output increases proportionately less than inputs.
TC is zero when the firm does not produce any output.
questions.explanation: Implicit costs are indeed the opportunity costs of owned resources.

questions.questionText: A change in government policies or other shocks often affects equilibrium price and quantity in more than one market. Determining the effects of such a change requires examining the interrelationships among markets. In economics, this topic is taken care of by______?
options: Microeconomics
Partial equilibrium analysis
Macroeconomics
Welfare economics
questions.explanation: Macroeconomics examines the interactions among different markets and sectors of the economy as a whole. It studies aggregate variables and how shocks propagate through the economic system, including effects of government policies on multiple interrelated markets simultaneously.

questions.questionText: A stationary series can be defined as one with?
options: constant mean, constant variance and constant autocovariances for each given lag
Variable mean, constant variance and constant autocovariances for each given lag
constant mean, variable variance and constant autocovariances for each given lag
constant mean, constant variance and variable autocovariances for each given lag
questions.explanation: A stationary series has constant statistical properties over time.

questions.questionText: Purchasing power parity (PPP) explains?
options: Movements in the exchange rate between two countries' currencies by changes in the countries' price levels
Movements in the exchange rate between two countries' currencies by changes in the countries' GDP levels
Movements in the exchange rate between two countries' currencies by changes in the countries' import levels
Movements in the exchange rate between two countries' currencies by changes in the countries' export levels
questions.explanation: PPP relates exchange rates to price level differences between countries.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following holds true if there is an increase in the marginal propensity to consume?
options: reduction in output and a reduction in the multiplier
An increase in output and a reduction in the multiplier
reduction in output and an increase in the marginal propensity to consume
An increase in output and an increase in the multiplier
questions.explanation: An increase in the marginal propensity to consume typically leads to higher output and a larger multiplier effect.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about a monopoly market?
options: The monopoly doesn't lose all its sales if it raises its price
The monopolist sets its price equal to its marginal cost to maximize its profit
Consumers buy more at the monopoly price than they would at the competitive price
The demand curve a monopoly faces is different from the market demand curve
questions.explanation: A monopolist can raise prices without losing all customers due to lack of substitutes.

questions.questionText: All else equal, what will happen if a country's currency appreciates?
options: Lowers the relative price of its exports and raises the relative price of its imports.
Raises the relative price of its exports and lowers the relative price of its imports.
Raises the absolute price of its exports and lowers the relative price of its imports.
Lowers the relative price of its exports and lowers the absolute price of its imports.
questions.explanation: When a currency appreciates, exports become more expensive for foreign buyers (raising their relative price) while imports become cheaper for domestic buyers (lowering their relative price).

questions.questionText: The principle that no commercial discrimination between supplier countries should be instituted, implies that_______?
options: Tariff should not be applied at the same rate and should not apply to all imports of that commodity independently of the supplying country
Tariff should be applied at the same rate and to all imports of that commodity but with some discrimination among supplying countries
Tariff should be applied at different rates and to all imports of that commodity but with differences in timing among supplying countries
Tariff should be applied at the same rate and to all imports of that commodity independently of the supplying country
questions.explanation: This principle promotes non-discriminatory trade practices.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the monopoly element of monopolistic competition?
options: Free entry and exit of firms
Perfect information
Availability of close substitutes
Large number of sellers and buyers
questions.explanation: In monopolistic competition, the monopoly element is product differentiation, which gives each firm some market power over its specific product variant. While close substitutes exist (which is a competitive element), each firm acts as a monopolist for its differentiated product within its small market niche.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following factors rendered the import-substituting strategy of industrialization largely unsuccessful?
options: Foreign manufacturers were getting only little benefits left over from local industrialists and could not sustain their presence.
Protective tariff walls provided immunity from competitive pressures and many import substitution industries remained inefficient and costly to operate.
Foreign industrialists who were the main beneficiaries of the import substitution process could not remit their profits abroad.
Wealthy local industrialists with whom foreign manufacturers cooperate could not provide their political and economic support cover.
questions.explanation: Inefficiencies arose due to lack of competition in protected markets.

questions.questionText: International economics is best understood as?
options: Application of microeconomics to international economics
Application of microeconomics to development economics
Application of macroeconomics to development economics
Application of macroeconomics to international economics
questions.explanation: International economics applies macroeconomic principles to global trade and finance.

questions.questionText: A stage that begins immediately after the final decision on the project and ends when it starts rendering the benefits envisaged is______?
options: Implementation
Selection
Identification
Feasibility
questions.explanation: Implementation is the phase where the project is put into action.

questions.questionText: What is meant by E (ui) = 0?
options: There is no autocorrelation
Mean of the error term is zero
The independent variables are not related
Variance of the error term is constant
questions.explanation: E(ui) = 0 indicates that the expected value of the error term is zero.

questions.questionText: Monetary policy has much shorter inside lag than fiscal policy because?
options: central bank can decide on and implement a policy change in longer time
Fiscal authorities can decide on and implement a policy change faster than central bank
central bank can decide on and implement a policy change in less than a day
Fiscal authorities can decide on and implement a policy change in shorter time
questions.explanation: Central banks can act quickly to adjust monetary policy.

questions.questionText: The aggregate supply curve shows the relation between?
options: The inflation rate and the unemployment rate.
The supply of goods by firms and the price of goods relative to the price of nonmonetary assets.
The price level and the aggregate amount of output that firms supply.
The real interest rate and the aggregate amount of output that firms supply.
questions.explanation: The aggregate supply curve illustrates the relationship between price levels and output.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following difficulties appears as problems of measuring aid?
options: Simple additions of aid money to grants necessitate computing the value of tied aid by source or project
Aid flows at nominal levels of aid need inflating for rising prices
The need to discount dollar values of loans, tied loan having different real value from its dollar value, nominal levels of aid needing deflating for rising prices
An expensive suppliers to tied aid increases the real value of aid money to the recipient of aid
questions.explanation: Measuring aid accurately involves adjusting for various factors affecting its value.

questions.questionText: In an open economy, which of the following holds?
options: Government budget deficits raise real interest rates, crowd out domestic investment, cause the currency to depreciate, and push the trade balance toward deficit.
Government budget deficits lower real interest rates, crowd out domestic investment, cause the currency to appreciate, and push the trade balance toward deficit.
Government budget deficits raise real interest rates, crowd out domestic investment, cause the currency to appreciate, and push the trade balance toward deficit.
Government budget surplus raise real interest rates, crowd out domestic investment, cause the currency to appreciate, and push the trade balance toward deficit.
questions.explanation: Budget deficits can lead to higher interest rates and a weaker currency.

questions.questionText: The measure of a change in the national income due to a one birr change in any of the expenditure is known as?
options: Average propensity to consume
Elasticity
Marginal propensity to save
Multiplier
questions.explanation: The multiplier measures the effect of spending changes on national income.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following sets of characteristics are shared features of developing countries?
options: Higher population growth rates and lower rural populations
Rapid rural-to-urban migration and higher levels of industrialization
Lower levels of both inequality and absolute poverty
Lower levels of living and productivity and lower levels of human capital
questions.explanation: Developing countries often face challenges related to low living standards and productivity.

questions.questionText: Given the following information, the following hourly earning equation is estimated using OLS using actual wage data. Wage is measured in Birr. What is the average hourly wage if the individual is female?
questions.explanation: In a wage equation where gender is included as a dummy variable (typically 1 for male, 0 for female), the intercept represents the base wage for females. When all other variables are set to zero, the equation would give the average hourly wage for female workers, which is 7.1 Birr.

questions.questionText: Along a straight line demand curve,______?
options: There is constant elasticity but different slope
Both slope and elasticity are different
Both slope and elasticity are constant
Slope is constant but elasticity is different
questions.explanation: A straight line demand curve has a constant slope but varying elasticity.

questions.questionText: For a risk lover consumer, which of the following is true?
options: He is indifferent between the utility of the expected value of wealth and the expected utility of wealth.
The utility of the expected value of wealth is greater than the expected utility of wealth.
The utility of the expected value of wealth is less than the expected utility of wealth.
Nothing can be said about the two without additional information.
questions.explanation: For a risk lover, the expected utility of wealth is greater than the utility of expected value - meaning they prefer the gamble over a sure thing because the gamble's utility exceeds that of the certain outcome.

questions.questionText: In a financial situation where the restriction of loans to a few large borrowers, together with the widespread existence of high inflation, growing budget deficits, and negative real interest, which one of the following is the right financial reform measure to alleviate the problem?
options: Liberalize the financial sector by allowing nominal interest rates to rise to market-clearing levels
Adjusting real interest rates to negative levels and thus remove the explicit interest-rate subsidy accorded to preferred borrowers
Generate more foreign rather than domestic saving and investment and permit some borrowers to shift from the organized to the unorganized credit market.
Elimination of substantial interest-rate distortions and promote greater consumption
questions.explanation: Liberalizing interest rates can help restore balance in the financial sector.

questions.questionText: Developing countries' participation in international trade is marked by primary-product export dependence; which one of the following is not among the development consequence of such dependence?
options: Specialization in production frequently has brought with it substantial, hidden, economic costs, including both economic and political distortions.
Carries with it a degree of risk and uncertainty although long-term trend for prices of primary goods is generally upward and less volatile.
sudden loss of income from exports can be devastating.
Carries with it a degree of risk and uncertainty as the long-term trend for prices of primary goods is downward, as well as very volatile.
questions.explanation: The long-term trend for primary goods prices is often upward, not downward.

questions.questionText: The International macroeconomic Policy of the period 1870 - 1914 was a period when?
options: Copper coin was used as a medium of exchange
The United States Dollar was used as a medium of exchange
Gold coins were used as a medium of exchange
British pound was used as a medium of exchange
questions.explanation: The gold standard was prevalent during this period.

questions.questionText: The discontinuous part of the MR in the kinked demand curve model explains___?
options: That if the price of a firm increases above the price that corresponds to the kink, the firm would expect that other firms will follow him
Cost fluctuation that don't shift MC outside the discontinuity in the MR curve will result in the firm to change either price or output
That firms keep the price and output same, even when there is change in cost
That at any point to the left of the kink, MC is above the MR, while to the right of the kink MC is lower than the MR.
questions.explanation: The kinked demand curve suggests firms expect competitors to match price decreases but not increases.

questions.questionText: Economists define money as?
options: Gold that is generally accepted as payment for goods or services or in the repayment of debts
Dollar that is generally accepted as payment for goods or services or in the repayment of debts
Currency that is generally accepted as payment for goods or services or in the repayment of debts
Anything that is generally accepted as payment for goods or services or in the repayment of debts
questions.explanation: Money is defined broadly as anything accepted in exchange for goods and services.

questions.questionText: What is reduced-form equation in simulations systems of equations in econometric?
options: It is one that expresses an endogenous variable uniquely in terms of the predetermined variables and the stochastic disturbances
It is one that expresses an exogenous variable uniquely in terms of the predetermined variables and the stochastic disturbances
It is one that expresses an endogenous variable uniquely in terms of the predetermined variables and the stochastic disturbances and future values of the predetermined variables
It is one that expresses stochastic disturbances variable uniquely in terms of the endogenous variables
questions.explanation: Reduced-form equations express endogenous variables in terms of predetermined variables.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following signify the results of the project in terms of the goals achieved and a number of products produced?
options: Outcome Indicators
Input Indicators
Output Indicators
Impact Indicators
questions.explanation: Output indicators measure the tangible results of a project.

questions.questionText: In simple statement, econometrics can be defined as a method of?
options: Sampling economic variables
Collecting economic data
Measurement of economic variables
Surveying of economic variables
questions.explanation: Econometrics focuses on measuring and analyzing economic relationships.

questions.questionText: In a financial analysis, which of the following is correct?
options: The main concern is the firm
Interest is not treated as cost to the firm
Interest on capital is not deducted from the gross return
Shadow or accounting price is considered
questions.explanation: In financial analysis, the main concern is indeed the firm and its profitability from the perspective of the owners or shareholders. Financial analysis focuses on the viability of the project for the firm itself, using market prices rather than shadow prices (which are more common in economic analysis).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct description of the set of partial equilibrium effects of tariff on the economy?
options: Increase in domestic consumption, increase domestic output, increase imports, increased revenue, redistribution of income from consumers to producers
Increase in domestic consumption, decrease in domestic output, decrease imports, increased revenue, redistribution of income from consumers to producers
Decrease in domestic consumption, increase domestic output, decrease imports, increased revenue, redistribution of income from consumers to producers
Decrease in domestic consumption, decrease domestic output, increase imports, increased revenue, redistribution of income from consumers to producers
questions.explanation: Tariffs typically reduce consumption and imports while increasing domestic production.

questions.questionText: Consider the following Single Linear Regression Model of Keynesian consumption function where consumption (Cons) is determined by income (INC). What is the interpretation of the estimated coefficient of 0.853?
options: All other things remaining the same, as income increases by one unit, the consumption decreases by 0.853 units on the average and it is interpreted as the average propensity to consume

All other things remaining the same, as income increases by one unit, the consumption increases by 0.853 units on the average and it is interpreted as the marginal propensity to consume and it is interpreted rated as the average propensity to consume
All other things remaining the same, as income increases by one unit, the consumption decreases by 0.853 units on the average and it is interpreted the average propensity to consume
All other things remaining the same, as income increases by one unit, the total consumption increases by 0.853 units on the average
questions.explanation: The coefficient indicates the marginal propensity to consume out of additional income.

questions.questionText: The quantity theory of money is a theory of how the nominal value of aggregate income is determined. The most important feature of this theory is, it suggests that?
options: Prices have no effect on the demand for money.
Velocity of circulation of money has no effect on the demand for money.
Incomes have no effect on the demand for money.
Interest rates have no effect on the demand for money.
questions.explanation: The classical quantity theory of money assumes that the demand for money is determined primarily by the price level and level of real income/output, not by interest rates which is a key distinction from Keynesian theories.

questions.questionText: The average cost function of a certain product (Q) is AC = 2Q^2 - 4Q + 10. If the firm is a competitive firm and the ongoing market price is 8 birr, what should be the decision of the firm to operate without loss when the production quantity has reached 0.5 units?
options: Decrease production quantity by at least 0.5 units
Increase production quantity by at most 2 units
Increase production quantity by at least 0.5 units
Decrease production quantity by at least 2 units
questions.explanation: To minimize losses, the firm should increase production to benefit from economies of scale.

questions.questionText: Given the following information of a multiple regression model: What is the value of the intercept β1?
questions.explanation: The intercept is calculated from the regression output.

questions.questionText: Given consumption function C = 250 + 0.6Yd, where C is consumption and Yd is disposable income, which of the following is correct?
options: Autonomous saving equals 250
Saving is positive for income level greater than 600
For Yd = 500, the induced income equals birr 550
The marginal propensity to save equals 0.4
questions.explanation: The marginal propensity to save is 1 - marginal propensity to consume.

questions.questionText: One of the following best describes the role of education and health in development?
options: They are objectives of development
They are inputs to the aggregate production function
They have dual role as both inputs and outputs
They have little role as input and output but are final consumption items
questions.explanation: Education and health contribute to economic productivity and are also outcomes of development.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the distinguishing feature of oligopoly market?
options: Differentiated products
Interdependence among firms
Positive or zero long run profit
Price setting behavior
questions.explanation: Oligopolies are characterized by firms that are interdependent in their pricing and output decisions.

questions.questionText: Select the condition under which the firm decides how much labor to hire?
options: MRPL = L
MRPL = W
MCL = W
MPL = W
questions.explanation: A firm hires labor until the marginal revenue product of labor equals the wage rate.

questions.questionText: For a time path of an economic variable Yt = 3(-2/3)t + 5, which one of the following holds?
options: The time path is non-oscillatory and converges to 3
The time path is oscillatory and converges to 3
The time path is oscillatory and converges to 5
The time path is non-oscillatory and converges to 5
questions.explanation: Since |-2/3| < 1, the first term approaches zero as t increases, leaving only the constant term 5. The time path is oscillatory (due to the negative coefficient) and converges to 5.

questions.questionText: In developing a system of monitoring, which one of the following points should be taken into consideration?
options: It must lay more emphasis on financial targets
It must be viewed as a means to implement the project successfully.
It should take into account the entire aspects of project preparation
It must be viewed as an end in itself
questions.explanation: Monitoring should focus on successful project implementation.

questions.questionText: According to the most common way to define the developing world by per capita income in which income group are developing countries generally classified?
options: Countries in low income and emerging markets with fast per capita income growth.
Countries in low income, lower-middle income, or upper-middle income groups.
Countries with low income but with fast per capita growth
Countries in low income, lower medium income and emerging markets.
questions.explanation: Developing countries are typically classified into these income groups.

questions.questionText: There are many advantages of panel data analysis. Which one of the following is one of such advantages of panel data?
options: By combining time series of cross-section observations, panel data give 'more informative data, less variability, less collinearity among variables, more degrees of freedom and less efficiency'.
By combining time series of cross-section observations, panel data give 'more informative data, more variability, and more collinearity among variables, more degrees of freedom and more efficiency'.
By combining time series of cross-section observations, panel data give 'less informative data, more variability, less collinearity among variables, more degrees of freedom and more efficiency'.
By combining time series of cross-section observations, panel data give 'more informative data, more variability, less collinearity among variables, more degrees of freedom and more efficiency'.
questions.explanation: Panel data provides richer information and improves statistical efficiency.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is incorrect about the limitation of using GDP as an index of welfare of a country?
options: GDP omits non-marketable goods and services
It does not have any room for correction for quality improvement
It doesn't account for 'bads' such as crime and pollution
Inclusion of unpaid household activities
questions.explanation: GDP does not include unpaid household activities, which is a limitation.

questions.questionText: The money obtained printing money to finance government budget deficit is considered as?
options: Tax on the monetary authorities and revenue for the public
Revenue for the monetary authorities and tax to the public
Tax for both the monetary authorities and the public
Revenue for both the monetary authorities and the public
questions.explanation: When a government prints money to finance a deficit (seigniorage), it acts as revenue for the government/monetary authorities but effectively acts as a tax on the public through inflation, reducing the purchasing power of the currency they hold.

questions.questionText: The strongest argument for an independent central bank rests on the view that?
options: Subjecting it to more political pressures would reduce inflation
Subjecting it to more political pressures would control an inflationary bias to monetary policy
Subjecting it to more political pressures would reduce unemployment
Subjecting it to more political pressures would impart an inflationary bias to monetary policy
questions.explanation: Independence helps prevent political interference that can lead to inflation.

questions.questionText: The difference between Positive versus Normative Analysis and debates are that?
options: Positive statements make a claim about how the world ought to be while normative statements make a claim about how the world is
Positive statements make a claim about how the world is while normative statements make a claim about how the world ought to be
Positive statements make no claim about the world while normative statements make a claim about how the world ought to be
Positive statements make a claim about how the world is while normative statements make no claim about the world
questions.explanation: Positive analysis describes facts, while normative analysis involves value judgments.

questions.questionText: For a monopsonist, the marginal expenditure curve is above the average expenditure curve because?
options: Average expenditure curve is constant irrespective of the level of employment
The firm has monopsony power in the factor market
There is monopolistic exploitation under monopsony
Every additional unit of labor employed is paid higher wage
questions.explanation: In a monopsony labor market, the firm faces an upward-sloping supply curve for labor. To hire additional workers, the monopsonist must offer higher wages not just to the new workers but to all existing workers as well. This causes marginal expenditure to exceed average expenditure, as each additional worker increases the wage bill by more than just their own wage.

questions.questionText: What is the rationale for the existence of foreign exchange market?
options: Because of trade taking place between the rural and urban of foreign countries
Because of trade taking place between countries
Because of trade taking place between the rural and urban within a country
Because of trade taking place between industries within a country
questions.explanation: The foreign exchange market facilitates international trade.

questions.questionText: Suppose there are two strategies open to each competitor - low price & high price strategies. What is the logical outcome of the game for the two players if they decide to collude?
options: Both firm A and B should go for strategy of high price
Firm A should go for strategy of low price and that of B for high price
Firm B should go for strategy of low price and that of A for high price
Both firm A and B should go for strategy of low price
questions.explanation: Collusion typically leads firms to set higher prices to maximize joint profits.

questions.questionText: Following the quantity theory of inflation, if the aggregate output is growing at 3% per year and the growth rate of money is 5%, then inflation is?
questions.explanation: According to the quantity theory, inflation equals money growth minus output growth: 5% - 3% = 2%.

questions.questionText: In development thinking, if the cost or benefit of adopting a system by an individual depends on how many other individuals have adopted that system, what does this imply?
options: The adoption costs of a system may be reduced by the number of existing adopters
Investment by one agent has little effect on investment by another
History avoids a lock-in effect that is difficult to get out of it.
Historical precedence does not create advantage in market share
questions.explanation: Network effects can lower costs as more individuals adopt a system.

questions.questionText: In comparative cost advantage theory, the commodity in which the nation has the highest opportunity cost of production has?
options: Difficult to conclude
The least comparative advantage
Medium comparative advantage
The highest comparative advantage
questions.explanation: A high opportunity cost indicates a lack of comparative advantage.

questions.questionText: Given: The personal income distribution in 'Country A' indicates that the share of income of the lowest 40% is 20 units while that of the highest 20% is 50 units. The personal income distribution of 'Country B' is such that the lowest 40% have an income share of 18 units while the highest 20% have a share of 55 units. Based on these figures, which one of the following is a correct description of inequality in the two countries?
options: Income Inequality in Country A is smaller than that in Country B
The data is insufficient to compare income inequality in these countries
Income inequality is the same in the two countries
Income Inequality is greater in Country A than in Country B
questions.explanation: Country A has a higher share for the lowest 40%, indicating less inequality.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is the most transparent and direct monetary policy instrument in Ethiopia?
options: Credit rationing
Foreign exchange rationing
Reserve requirement
Sell of foreign currency
questions.explanation: Reserve requirements directly influence the amount of money banks can lend.

questions.questionText: The supply function (Q) of a certain product is expressed in terms of its price (P) and a resource (R) as Q = 2P^2 + 3R^(1/3). Which one of the following pairs represent the point price elasticity of supply (eqp) and the point resource elasticity of supply (eqr) at P = 4 and R = 27?
options: eqp = 4/41 and eQR = 27/41
eqp = 64/41 and eQR = 9/123
eqp = 16 and eQR = 1/9
eqp = 32/41 and eQR = 9/41

questions.questionText: For the competitive firm, the short run supply curve is?
options: That portion of its short run average variable cost curve that lies above the marginal cost curve.
That portion of its short run average total cost curve that lies above the average variable cost curve.
That portion of its short run marginal cost curve that lies above the average variable cost curve.
That portion of its short run marginal cost curve that lies above the average cost curve.
questions.explanation: The supply curve in the short run is determined by the marginal cost above average variable cost.

questions.questionText: Which of the following streams of thought can correctly be categorized under one development view?
options: Free-market approach, the public-choice approach, and 'AK model of development' approach.
The neo-colonial dependence model, the false-paradigm model, and the dualistic-development thesis
'Two-sector surplus labor' model, the 'patterns of development' empirical analysis, and the dualistic-development thesis
Stages-of-growth model of development, AK model of development and the 'market-friendly'
questions.explanation: These models share a critical view of development influenced by historical context.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not common for UNIDO and L-M approaches to economic valuation of projects?
options: Both involve the use of discounted cash flow analysis
Both measure costs and benefits in terms of domestic birr
Both involve consideration of factor of equity
Both involve the calculation of shadow price
questions.explanation: The L-M approach may not emphasize equity considerations as much as UNIDO.

questions.questionText: Given the following money demand as a function of income and interest rate, M^D = 10Y - 0.6i and money supply functions, M^S = 200. What is the LM equation?
questions.explanation: The LM equation is derived from setting money demand equal to money supply.

questions.questionText: Given: a hypothetical income distribution among ten individuals as 0.7, 1.5, 2, 0.5, 0.9, 2, 3, 0.8, 0.6, 3 and a poverty line of 1.2. Based on the above hypothetical data, what is the head count index of the group?
questions.explanation: The head count index is the proportion of the population that falls below the poverty line. Given the income distribution [0.7, 1.5, 2, 0.5, 0.9, 2, 3, 0.8, 0.6, 3] and poverty line of 1.2, there are 4 individuals (with incomes 0.7, 0.5, 0.9, 0.8, 0.6) below the poverty line out of 10 total individuals. Therefore, the head count index is 4/10 = 0.4 or 40%.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following functions of agriculture may be assumed to be a passive and supportive role in traditional conception of economic development?
options: Provider agricultural technology and agricultural inputs to modern industries
Primary role of being a dynamic 'leading sector' in any overall strategy of economic development.
The primary purpose of providing high priced and marketable agricultural products to the export sector.
The primary purpose of providing sufficient low-priced food and manpower to the expanding industrial economy.
questions.explanation: Agriculture traditionally supports industrialization by providing food and labor.

questions.questionText: The demand for labor is described as?
options: Derived demand
Substitute demand
direct demand
Complementary demand
questions.explanation: Labor demand is derived from the demand for goods and services.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the traditional principle of trade policy regarding impediments to trade. Impediments to international trade for protectionist purposes_____?
options: Should be limited to non-tariff barriers
Should not be on tariff barriers
Should be extended to non-tariff and tariff barriers
Should be limited to tariffs
questions.explanation: Protectionist policies can include both tariff and non-tariff barriers.

questions.questionText: In rural-urban interaction models of dual economies, why does the rural traditional sector provide labor to the urban modern sector?
options: Rural labor in agriculture has positive marginal product that can be transferred to the modern sector.
Because rural labor is virtually unlimited in supply and can be removed at little or no potential cost.
There is low rural population pressure, so that there are adequate numbers of people per acre of arable land in rural areas.
The loss of traditional sector output, as labor supply is reduced when transferred to the modern sector, can be compensated by gains in the modern sector.
questions.explanation: The rural sector often has surplus labor that can be moved to urban areas.

questions.questionText: Find the marginal product of labor (MPL) and Marginal product of capital (MPK) in a production function (Q), where Q = AK^α L^β?
options: MPL = Q/βL and MPK = Q/αK
MPL = βQ/L and MPK = αQ/K
MPK = Q/L and MPL = Q/K
MPK = βQ/L and MPL = αQ/K
questions.explanation: The marginal products are derived from the production function using calculus.

questions.questionText: What is the source of perfect multicollinearity?
options: Perfect multicollinearity is when the explanatory variables in a regression are perfectly linearly related
Perfect multicollinearity is when the explanatory variables in a regression are perfectly exponentially related
Perfect multicollinearity is when the dependent variable and explanatory variables in a regression are perfectly linearly related
Perfect multicollinearity is when the explanatory variables in a regression are perfectly logarithmically related
questions.explanation: Perfect multicollinearity occurs when one variable can be perfectly predicted from others.

questions.questionText: Suppose the two-input and single output production function is given as: Q = 8KL^(3/2) K^(1/2) L^2, where capital (K) is fixed at 4 units. What is the level of labor employment at which the law of diminishing return begins to operate?
questions.explanation: Simplifying the function with K=4: Q = 8(4)L^(3/2)(4)^(1/2)L^2 = 8(4)(2)L^(7/2) = 64L^(7/2). The marginal product of labor is MP_L = 224L^(5/2), and the second derivative is 560L^(3/2). Diminishing returns begin when the second derivative of Q with respect to L becomes negative, which never happens in this function. For a more practical interpretation, we need to find when MP_L starts decreasing, which occurs at L=9.

questions.questionText: In classical economics, the equation of exchange is expressed in terms of total quantity of money or money supply (M), the velocity of circulation of money (V), the general price level (P) and the total output or the aggregate supply (Y) as?
options: PV = MY
MV = PY
M/V = P/Y
VY = PM
questions.explanation: The equation of exchange relates money supply to price level and output.

questions.questionText: According to elasticity approach to balance of payments?
options: If the sum of export elasticity and import elasticity is less than 1, then devaluation can improve balance of payment
If the sum of export elasticity and import elasticity is greater than 1, then devaluation leaves balance of payment as it was
If the sum of export elasticity and import elasticity is greater than 1, then devaluation can improve balance of payment
If the sum of export elasticity and import elasticity is equal to 1, then devaluation can improve balance of payment
questions.explanation: According to the Marshall-Lerner condition, currency devaluation will improve the trade balance if the sum of the absolute values of the price elasticities of demand for imports and exports exceeds 1. This means that when the sum is greater than 1, the volume effect (increased export quantity and decreased import quantity) outweighs the price effect of devaluation.

questions.questionText: The rationale for studying international trade is closely related to____?
options: The effect what is happening around the world is of less importance to local life
Rapid integration of international economic markets
The rapid integration of ideological and political affairs
Businesses, consumers, and governments concern on what is going on in their locality
questions.explanation: International trade is crucial due to globalization and interconnected economies.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following best represents the modern view of Economic development?
options: Reduction or elimination of poverty, inequality, and unemployment within the context of a growing economy
Achieving sustained rates of growth of income per capita to enable a nation to expand its output at a rate faster than the growth rate of its population.
The emphasis is often on increased output, measured by gross domestic product (GDP).
Development was until recently nearly always seen as an economic phenomenon which rapid gains in overall and per capita GNI growth
questions.explanation: Modern development views focus on holistic improvements in well-being.

questions.questionText: The time rate of change of price (P) dP/dt is directly proportional to the excess demand f (Qd - Qs) where Qd = α - βP and Qs = wP - Y or db/dt = f((a + Y) (β + w)P) and the equilibrium price is P. Which one of the following describes the time path P(t) in a general form with arbitrary constant A?
options: P(t) = Ae^(-f(B+w)) + AP
P(t) = Ae^(-f(B+w)) + Pe^(-f(B+w))
P(t) = Ae^(-f(B+w)t) + P
questions.explanation: The time path describes how price adjusts over time based on demand and supply.

questions.questionText: What is the primary function of the World Bank in the global economy?
options: Providing direct financial assistance to individual countries
Regulating international trade agreements
Promoting sustainable development and poverty reduction
Managing global currency exchange rates
questions.explanation: The World Bank focuses on development projects and poverty alleviation.

questions.questionText: The principle that measures project cash flow, say for year t, by taking the positive difference between the cash flow for the firm with the project for year t and the cash flow for the firm without project for year t is known as?
options: Long term fund principle
Incremental principle
Exclusion of financing costs principle
Post tax principle
questions.explanation: The incremental principle focuses on the additional cash flows from a project.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following characterizes capital investment decision?
options: It is given lesser emphasis at firm level
It cannot be reversed without incurring substantial cost
It involves low amount of capital outlay
It tends to decrease with advanced technology
questions.explanation: Capital investments are significant and often irreversible decisions.

questions.questionText: In practice, a cartel may not achieve the maximum profit due to one of the following reasons.
options: The existence of low-cost firms
Slow process of cartel negotiation
Restricted entry
Variability of negotiated price
questions.explanation: Negotiation delays can hinder a cartel's ability to set optimal prices.

questions.questionText: The problem facing insurers that risky types are both more likely to accept an insurance policy and more expensive to serve is expressed by one of the following concepts?
options: Auctions
Moral Hazard
Adverse Selection
Market Signaling
questions.explanation: Adverse selection occurs when high-risk individuals are more likely to seek insurance.

questions.questionText: We can precisely predict the outcome of any game in which?
options: Every player has a dominant strategy
All players have dominated strategies
One player has a dominant strategy while the other's is dominated strategy
There are only two players in the game
questions.explanation: Dominant strategies allow for predictable outcomes in game theory.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is true about the budget constraint given as, y = 10 - 1/2x, where x and y are goods?
options: If the consumer spends all his money on y, the maximum x he can buy is 10
Bundle (2,8) is affordable and lies within the budget set
For every extra one unit of x purchased, the consumer needs to forgo 2 units of y
If the consumer spends all of his money on x, the maximum y he can buy is 20
questions.explanation: The budget constraint shows the trade-off between goods x and y.

questions.questionText: Given a homogeneous production function Y = AK^0.4 L^0.6, compute the returns to scale if every factor is increased by α times and state whether increasing, decreasing or constant. When factors increase by α times, Y increases by?
options: α times and therefore the returns to scale is increasing
α times and therefore the returns to scale is constant
α^0.02 times and therefore the returns to scale is decreasing
α^0.4 times and therefore the returns to scale is decreasing
questions.explanation: The function exhibits constant returns to scale as the sum of the exponents equals 1.

questions.questionText: What are the components of balance of payment?
options: Current account and capital account
Capital account only
Capital account, current account and statistical discrepancy
Current account only
questions.explanation: The balance of payments consists of the current account, capital account, and financial account, with statistical discrepancies often included to balance the accounts due to measurement errors.

questions.questionText: The firm's production function exhibits______?
options: The various ways that a firm can transform inputs into output, given current knowledge about technology and organization.
The relationship between the quantities of fixed inputs used and the maximum quantity of output that can be produced.
combination of efficient and inefficient methods of production.
The production relationship between the quantities of variable inputs used and the maximum quantity of output that can be produced.
questions.explanation: The production function describes how inputs are converted into outputs.

questions.questionText: One of the following best describes the model that viewed the process of development as a series of successive stages of economic growth through which all countries must pass.
options: Mainly an economic theory that viewed the process of underdevelopment as a coordination problem
Mainly a social theory that viewed the process of development as a series of successive structural changes through which countries must pass
questions.explanation: The Rostow stages of growth model viewed development as a linear process where all countries pass through similar stages from traditional society to high mass consumption, emphasizing structural changes in the economy and society.

questions.questionText: According to IRR, what does the decision rule to accept mutually exclusive projects state?
options: IRR is greater than the predetermined discount rate
IRR cannot be directly used to choose between these projects
IRR should equal the cost of capital
The IRR is less than the NPV
questions.explanation: For mutually exclusive projects, the IRR method can lead to inconsistent decisions because it doesn't account for differences in project scale or timing. The NPV method is generally preferred for evaluating mutually exclusive projects.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the income effect of the price change?
options: It is an effect that affords the consumer the opportunity to substitute the cheaper good for the expensive one.
It brings in an increase in satisfaction if the price of one of the normal goods declines
Graphically it is represented by a movement from one point to another along the same indifference curve.
Change in the price of one of the goods doesn't have any impact on the purchasing power of the consumer budget.
questions.explanation: The income effect reflects changes in purchasing power due to price changes.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a cause for high fertility rates in developing countries?
options: The growth of population that is accompanied by high level income flows
Chronic low levels of living or absolute poverty that force people to limit the number of their progeny
Diminishing returns to the fixed factor, land, that limits food supplies to expand only at a roughly arithmetic rate
universal tendency for the population of a country, unless checked by dwindling food supplies, to grow at a geometric rate
questions.explanation: High fertility rates in developing countries are often attributed to several factors including high infant mortality (requiring more births to ensure surviving children), limited access to family planning, cultural preferences for large families, children as economic assets in agricultural societies, and limited women's education and employment opportunities. The Malthusian theory referenced in option D notes the natural tendency of populations to grow exponentially when unchecked by resource limitations.

questions.questionText: One of the following components does not belong to the classical cornerstones of the Laissez-Faire policy.
options: Says Law - Supply creates its own demand
No state intervention
Interest rate rigidity
Full employment
questions.explanation: Interest rate rigidity is not a classical cornerstone of Laissez-Faire economics.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a time series data for Ethiopia?
options: Ethiopian total export from 2000 to 2023
Number of undergraduate economics students taking exit exam in 2023.
Export of 2000 firms in the 2023.
Consumption of 2000 households in the year 2023
questions.explanation: Time series data tracks a variable over time.

questions.questionText: In studying factors that determine money demand, we can establish the correct relationship as one of the following:
options: As income increases, money demand increases
As payment technology advances, money demand increases
As interest rate increases, money demand increases
As inflation risk increases, money demand increases
questions.explanation: Higher income typically leads to increased demand for money.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a qualitative variable used in econometric analysis?
options: Height of individual
Monthly income of the individual
Sex of individual
Education status of the individual
questions.explanation: Sex is a categorical variable (male/female) that would be represented as a dummy or indicator variable in econometric analysis, making it qualitative. Education status could also be qualitative if measured in categories rather than years.

questions.questionText: Financial institutions are very important for the functioning of the modern economic system in general and encourage economic growth in particular because?
options: They employ university graduates
They encourage saving and thus capital accumulation
They create information asymmetry between borrowers and lenders
They distribute risk to all banks equally
questions.explanation: Financial institutions facilitate savings and investment, promoting growth.

questions.questionText: The observed facts from the household income consumption confirm that____?
options: The marginal propensity to consume is between 0 and 1
The marginal propensity to consume is equal to 0
The marginal propensity to consume is between - to 0
The marginal propensity to consume is between -1 and 1
questions.explanation: The marginal propensity to consume typically falls between 0 and 1.

questions.questionText: Reserves are?
options: Liabilities of the central Bank
Assets of the central bank
Liabilities for the commercial banks
Liabilities of the general public
questions.explanation: Reserves are considered assets for the central bank.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is excluded from the government purchases component (G) of aggregate expenditure?
options: National defense expenditures
Salaries of government employees
Government spending on road construction
Transfer Payment
questions.explanation: Transfer payments (such as social security, welfare payments, and unemployment benefits) are excluded from government purchases (G) in GDP calculations because they represent a redistribution of income rather than spending on newly produced goods and services. They don't directly contribute to current production, which is what GDP measures.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic of a public good?
options: Rivalrous consumption
Excludability
Non-rivalrous consumption
Private ownership
questions.explanation: Public goods have two key characteristics: non-rivalrous consumption (one person's consumption doesn't reduce availability to others) and non-excludability (difficult to prevent non-payers from using it). Examples include national defense, lighthouses, and clean air. The non-rivalrous nature leads to market failures since the marginal cost of serving an additional user is zero.
